Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 
2024
Kabc020177202021
 In The Court Of The Xi Addl. Small Causes And
 Addl. Mact., Bangalore, (Scch-12)
 Present: Smt.Vidyalaxmi Bhat
 B.A, LLB(hon)L.L.M.
 Xi Addl. Small Causes Judge & Acmm,
 Court of Small Causes,
 Member, Mact12, Bengaluru. 
 Dated this the 19th day of March, 2024  MVC.No.2689/2021 Petitioner : Krishnappa.G  S/o Gopalappa  Aged about 36 years  Residing at #32  Near Yallamma Temple, Sompura  Bengaluru562125.
 (By Smt. Asha.A, Advocate)
 V/ s Respondent/s: 1. HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co.
 Ltd 'No.11, I Floor, H.M.Enclave, House  No.14, Cunningham Road,
 Bengaluru560052.
 (Policy No.2315203969892200000  Valid from 18.01.2021 to 17.01.2022)
 (Insurer of Vehicle No. KA01AF1238)
 2. Mr.H.P.Mehboob Pasha  S/o Syed Pachasab  R/at Rajapurapete  (SCCH12) 2 MVC 2689/2021  Hoskote, Bengaluru Rural  Bengaluru562114. 
 (Owner of Vehicle No.KA01AF1238) 
 (R1 By Sri.K.Suresh, Advocate) 
 (R2 Exparte) 
 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
1 Accident.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 14.06.2021 at about 8.00 pm when he was traveling in two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA51V9410 slowly cautiously and observing all traffic norms on Gunjur main road, Bengaluru when he came in front of Govt. Higher Primary School , at that time one Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF1238 driven by its driver came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner without caring for human safety dashed to the petitioner's vehicle. Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous all over his body. Immediately he was shifted to nearby Vydehi hospital and then to Kaveri Multi Specialty hospital for treatment. He underwent surgery and discharged with medical advice and for regular follow up treatment. He has spent more than 3,00,000/ towards medical expenses, attendance charges, food and nourishment. 
3. Prior to accident he was hale and healthy. He was aged 36 years and was a 'Driver' by profession and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month. Due to the accident he lost all his income and suffered physical and mental stress. That complaint is lodged before Whitefield Police Station in Cr.No.35/2021 under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC. The 2 nd respondent is the R.C.owner and 1st respondent is the insurer of offending vehicle. They are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest @ 12% pa in the above case. 
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.2 remained absent on the date of hearing therefore, he is placed exparte. Respondent no.1 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further it seeks protection under section 147 and 149 of M.V.Act 1988. As per section 134 (c) of Motor Vehicle Act it is mandatory duty of the insured to furnish the particulars of policy, date, time and place of alleged accident, particulars of injuries and the name of the driver etc and he has not complied the same. That policy have not complied the provision of Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicle Act. Further stated that the 2nd respondent has entrusted the vehicle knowingly to a person who had no valid and effective driving license and thereby committed breach of contract and violation of terms and conditions of the policy as on the date of alleged accident. That insured vehicle had no permit and FC as on the date of accident. That Canter in question did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and the said injuries sustained is due to self fall from motor cycle bearing No.KA51V9410 which he was riding and the canter vehicle is falsely implicated to have caused accident. That petition is bad for nonjoinder of proper and necessary parties to the petition. Permission sought to contest the above claim petition under Sec 170 of Motor Vehicle Act if the owner fails to cooperate with this respondent. The negligence on part of the canter driver is denied. The involvement of aforesaid vehicle in the accident is denied. The medical treatment taken by the petitioner are denied. The age, occupation, income and permanent disability alleged by the petitioner all are denied. The medical expenses borne by the petitioner are denied. On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition. 
5. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:
ISSUES Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
2 1. Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 14.06.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF 1238 when it hit his two wheeler bearing No.KA51V9410? 
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any? 
3. Whether the 1st respondent proves that the driver of driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA01 AF 1238 did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident? 
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so by whom and what is the quantum? 
5. What Order or Award? 
6. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1. Ex.P.1 to P.13 documents are marked on his behalf. In cross examination of P.W.1, on confrontation by respondent no.1 Ex.R.1 is marked. On the contrary to prove the defence the authorized representative of respondent no.1 is examined as R.W.1 and Ex.R.2 is marked, and respondent evidence is closed. 
7. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
8. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3: In the Negative, Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : According to the petitioner he sustained injuries due to the accident occurred on 14.06.2021 in which Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF1238 hit his two wheeler and he sustained injuries. To prove his case, he himself entered into witness box and got examined as P.W.1. In chief examination he reiterated petition averments and further stated that even after taking best available treatment he is still suffering from disability. To prove the accidental injuries and negligence on the part of Canter driver he produced FIR, first information, spot panchanama, IMV report, sketch, final report, wound certificate and discharge summary at Ex.P.1 to 9. They show that complaint was given by the friend of petitioner stating that his fatherinlaw sustained injuries in the accident occurred on 14.06.2021 at 8.00 pm when he was traveling on two wheeler and one Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF1238 hit the rider of two wheeler. Such first information was given on 15.06.2021 that is one day after the accident. The canter number is mentioned in the first information. IMV report says that front right side bumpers scratched to the canter and head lamp assembly damaged and left side indicator damaged in respect of two wheeler. FIR is registered against the driver of the canter and in the final report also name of the driver of the canter is mentioned and offence u/s 279 and 338 of IPC is registered against the driver of the canter. In the Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
3 wound certificate given by Dr. Kiran.J, Kaveri Specialty hospital it is mentioned that alleged history of RTA on 14.06.2021 and there is fracture of right maxillary and right temporal bone which is grievous in nature. 
In the discharge summary produced at Ex.P.8 it is mentioned that there is history of RTA on 14.06.2021. It is also mentioned that patients attender has given history of the injury as two wheeler rider accidentally hitting the barricade following which patient had a lateral collision with 4 wheeler and sustained injury to head on the left side. Further in the history it is also mentioned that patient was under influence of alcohol as per the history given by the attender. 
10. As per Ex.P.8 petitioner was admitted to hospital on the same night of the accident at 10.29 pm and discharged immediately after one hour at 11.38 pm. he was then shifted to Kaveri Speciality hospital and MLC extract given by Kaveri hospital is admitted by P.W.1 and marked as Ex.R.1. In the MLC extract of Kaveri hospital, it is mentioned that alleged history of RTA, rider hit by car, patient was under influence of alcohol, near Gunjur at 6.00 pm on 14.06.2021. 
11. 1st respondent contended that it is a case of self fall and relied upon the judgment in Gurappa V/s Gowdappa Gowda and another, 2009 ACJ 293 and Vijay V.Shetty V/s V.Sharada and others,
ILR 2015 KAR 401. In the first of those cases, pillion sustained injuries and before doctor it was stated that she slipped from the steps and sustained head injury and therefore claim petition was rejected. In the 2 nd decision injury was caused due to skid of the vehicle and self fall from the bike. 
In the present case, in the MLC extract there is mention about 4 wheeler. Therefore, it cannot be considered as purely a self fall case. The decisions relied by the 1 st respondent cannot be made applicable to the case on hand. 
12. Further it is necessary to notice that inpatient record of Kaveri hospital is not produced. Medical test report of the petitioner showing that he was under the influence of alcohol is not produced. 
Further in the final report there is no allegation on the petitioner that he was riding two wheeler under the influence of alcohol. Therefore, only on the basis of history given by the attender of the patient that, patient was under the influence of alcohol, court cannot come to the conclusion that,
petitioner was under the influence of alcohol at the time of riding the two wheeler, more particularly in the absence of any supporting medical test report regarding presence of alcohol. Therefore, in the opinion of this court though respondent no.2 contended that, it is self fall case under the influence of alcohol, the same cannot be accepted. In the cross examination of P.W.1 he denied that he was drunken and driving the two wheeler. When he denied such suggestion, burden is on the 2 nd respondent to prove the said fact. One who avers must prove the fact. In the present case 2 nd respondent only averred that petitioner was under the influence of alcohol, but not proved the same. 
Therefore, the said fact is not proved. 
13. The police documents and medical reports in respect of the accident and injuries are not questioned by the accused, canter driver. The material suggestions that false case is filed by the petitioner are denied by P.W.1 in the cross examination. 
Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
4 Therefore in the absence of any contrary material, the case of the petitioner cannot be disbelieved. 
In the Ex.R.5 sketch produced by petitioner it can be seen that accident took place on the left side of the road from Varthuru side towards Gunjuru side, petitioner was traveling from Varthuru side towards Gunjuru and he was on left side of the road, canter came to the right side and hit the petitioner. Therefore, there is negligence on part of the canter driver. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence, this court comes to the conclusion that petitioner has proved that he sustained injuries in the road traffic accident dated 14.06.2021 by negligent driving of the Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF1238. Accordingly, I hold this point in the Affirmative. 
14. ISSUE NO.2 : Respondent no.1 disputed the age of the petitioner in the written statement. To prove his age petitioner has not produced any document in evidence, but at the time of filing petition he ha produced his aadhaar card which shows that he was born on 04.05.1985. As on the date of accident 14.06.2021 he was aged 36 years. Respondent no.1 has not produced any other document to disprove the age. Therefore, age of the petitioner is considered as 36 years at the time of accident. 
15. 1st respondent disputed the occupation of the petitioner. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner is Driver. He has not produced any document. Since no documents are produced regarding occupation, notional income has to be considered to decide the income of petitioner. 
16. 1st respondent disputed income of the petitioner. According to petitioner he was earning Rs.20,000/ per month from his occupation. To prove this fact, he has not produced any document. 
Therefore, notional income has to be inferred. As per the judgment in Smt. Mariyamma and others V/s Suyambulingam.V. and another, MFA 7404/2014 dated 06.12.2022 the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that tribunal has to consider the provisions of Minimum Wages Act to decide notional income. The relevant notification as on the date of accident under the aforesaid Act is not produced by the petitioner. Further it is held in the above said case that provisions of Minimum Wages Act are beckon only and it need not be like with mathematical precision. Therefore in the opinion of this court petitioner's earning has to be considered as Rs.14,000/ per month. Hence monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.14,000/. In respect of permanent disability,
petitioner not got examined any doctor. Hence, permenant disability is not proved. Accordingly I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative. 
17. Issue no.3: 1st respondent contended that driver of the Canter was not having driving licence at the time of accident, but no documents are produced to prove the said fact. Hnce, mere averment that opponent vehicle driver had no D.L itself is not sufficient to prove the defence. Therefore, this issue is not proved by the 1st respondent. Hence, I hold this issue in the Negative. 
18. Issue no.4: In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the Canter bearing reg.No.KA01AF1238. There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident. Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents. The records show that he underwent operation for facial injuries as per Ex.P9 discharge summary and he is discharged against medical advice. He was in hospital from 15.06.2021 to 22.06.2021 for 8 days. Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
5 compensation of Rs.30,000/ . 
19. The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.10. He has taken treatment at Vaidehi and Kaveri hospitals. As per Ex.P.10 medical bill, petitioner has paid Rs.2,34,030/. The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him. They are subsequent to the date of accident. They are disputed by respondent, but no satisfactory material is placed to disprove the bills or any payment made by any other medical insurance. Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.2,34,030/.
20. The petitioner was in hospital for 8 days. Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded. Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.300/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice. Hence for food and nourishment Rs.300/
x 8 days = Rs.2,400/is awarded. 
21. For a period of inpatient for 8 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital. 
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost. Hence attendant charges has to be awarded. if per day Rs.300/ is awarded as attendant charges in 2021, it will meet the ends of justice. Hence for attendant charges Rs.300/ x 8 days =Rs.2,400/is awarded. 
22. As per the above findings, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.14,000/. The minimum period of recovery in case of grievous injury can be considered as 3 months and therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.14,000/x 3 = 42,000/ He is entitled to Rs.42,000/ as loss of income during laid up period. 
23. It is stated that petitioner was shifted from spot of accident to the hospital. He took treatment at Vaidehi and Kaeri hospitals. He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment. 
Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice. Accordingly, Rs.5,000/ is awarded. 
24. Since doctor is not examined and permanent disability and requirement of future medical treatment is not established, petitioner is not entitled for loss of future income due to disability compensation for future medical treatment. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Pain & Sufferings 30,000/
ii. Medical expenses 2,34,030/
iii. Food and nourishment 2,400/
iv. Attendant charges 2,400/
v. Loss of income during laid up 42,000/
 period vi. Conveyance charges 5,000/ 
Krishnappa.G vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 19 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63105720/
6 vii. Loss of income due to disability nil viii. Future medical expenses nil  Total Rs.3,15,830/ 
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.3,15,830/ in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident. 
25. Liability: Since respondent no.1 has admitted the insurance policy of Canter bearing reg.no.KA 01AF1238 which is valid on the date of accident, he is liable to indemnify the insured. As per settled law on the point of interest, though petitioner claimed interest at the rate of 12% pa he is only entitled to 6% interest on the award amount. Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. ISSUE NO.5: In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs. It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,15,830/ with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment. 
 The respondent no.1 insurance  company is liable to indemnify the  insured and directed to deposit the  aforesaid compensation amount with  interest within two months from the date  of this order. 
 After such deposit, the petitioner is  entitled to have release of entire compensation after proper identification.
 The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Award be drawn accordingly. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced in the Open Court on this 19th day of March, 2024) (Vidyalaxmi Bhat) XI Addl. Small Causes Judge and ACMM, Bangalore.

7 Discharge summary issued by Kaveri hospital Ex.P.10 Medical bills (33 nos) Ex. P.11 Final bill of Kaveri hospital Ex . P.12 Final bill of Vaidehi hospital Ex . P.13 Prescriptions and lab reports(39nos) Witnesses examined for the respondents :
R.W.1 Suresh.G. Documents marked for the respondents : Ex.R.1 M.L.C register extract Ex.R.2 Copy of insurance policy (Vidyalaxmi Bhat), XI Addl. Small Causes Judge and ACMM, Bangalore.
